comparison: Perfect agreement on study cohort characteristics (C81-C86, C99-C102). Both evaluations support these methodological details without concerns, though peer reviewers note limitations like lack of racial diversity.
Perfect agreement on longitudinal resolution of T-cell activation (C45-C49, C96). Both evaluations support the temporal normalization by 12 months as convincing evidence.
Perfect agreement on antigen-specific immune responses (C59-C62). Both evaluations support the ELISpot and antibody data showing robust responses across severity groups.
Perfect agreement on functional T-cell characterization (C63-C71). Both evaluations support the ICS data showing differences in magnitude but not quality of responses.
Perfect agreement on Ki67 expression and bystander activation (C72-C73). Both evaluations support this finding as evidence for IL-15-driven mechanisms.

Perfect agreement on symptom burden data (C7, C74-C76). Both evaluations support the finding that severe patients have higher symptom counts, though peer reviewers request more granular outcome measures.
Perfect agreement on negative viral detection (C90). Both evaluations support this finding as ruling out persistent viral replication as a driver of activation.

Strong agreement on background literature and contextual claims (C1-C2, C10-C26, C87-C89, C91-C92, C94-C95, C97-C98). Both evaluations support these as appropriate contextualization, with peer reviewers suggesting minor additions about vaccine protection.

Divergent evaluations on statistical associations between immune activation and symptoms (C8-C9, C77-C80). OpenEval supports the findings and conclusions as appropriately qualified, while peer reviewers express uncertainty and request reanalysis with more specific PASC outcome measures.
Agreement on IL-15Rα upregulation and mechanistic interpretation (C5-C6, C57-C58). Both evaluations support the co-culture experiment data and the bystander activation hypothesis.

Divergent evaluations on cytokine data interpretation (C4, C51-C53). OpenEval supports the findings as statistically significant with appropriate testing, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about biological significance and request context from other diseases.
Agreement on normalization of standard inflammatory markers (C27, C93). Both evaluations support this finding, with peer reviewers suggesting minor presentation improvements for temporal comparisons.

Strong agreement on CD4+ T-cell activation findings (C3, C29-C30, C32, C34-C36). Both evaluations support the flow cytometry data as convincing evidence, though OpenEval also includes additional claims (C27-C28, C31, C33) not explicitly addressed in peer review.
Agreement on longitudinal cytokine kinetics (C54-C56). Both evaluations support these temporal patterns as complementary data, with no specific concerns raised.

Strong agreement on CD8+ T-cell activation findings (C38-C39, C41, C43-C44). Both evaluations support the flow cytometry data, though OpenEval also includes claims C37, C40, C42 not explicitly addressed in peer review.

Agreement on CD80 expression differences (C50). Both evaluations support this minor finding, with OpenEval noting it as statistically significant and peer reviewers accepting it as baseline immunological context.
Agreement on baseline immunological parameters showing no differences (C37, C40). Both evaluations support these findings as providing context for observed activation differences.
Agreement on baseline parameters (C28, C31). Both evaluations support these findings showing no differences across severity groups at baseline.
Agreement on mechanistic interpretation of IL-15-driven bystander activation (C6). Both evaluations support this interpretation as reasonable and grounded in experimental data and literature.

Divergent evaluations on main study conclusions (C9). OpenEval supports the conclusion as appropriately qualified, while peer reviewers express uncertainty due to concerns about outcome measure specificity.
Agreement on literature supporting IL-15 mechanisms (C87-C89). Both evaluations accept these citations as appropriate background for the bystander activation hypothesis.
Agreement on normalization of inflammatory markers (C27). Both evaluations support this finding as part of the temporal resolution pattern.
Agreement on study conclusions and context (C98). Both evaluations accept the main conclusions, though peer reviewers request more specific outcome measures that may affect interpretation.
